note: ADR-0011 §3.2 and §3.3. The triode stage is held to an ngspice simulation of the same netlist (tests/spice/, made by the SPICE reference harness): operating point, fundamental, and every harmonic up to 20 kHz at or above spice.floor_dbc, at the default quality's oversampled rates; the processor's harmonic levels through the oversampler at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz. Aliasing (non-harmonic energy in 20 Hz-20 kHz on tones from 1 to 19 kHz at the nominal drive, the default drive with a -18 dBFS tone, the EBU R68 alignment level): §3.2's -90 dBc for the default quality, -70 dBc for eco; hotter levels are reported. The zipper tone is -40 dBFS, so full drive stays clean enough that the harmonics are not read as steps; the bar moves with it (checks.cpp). Hot input (squares at 0, +12 and +24 dBFS, drive +36 dB, every quality): output within the stage's range and every block inside the 2.67 ms period (the RT audit of PR #52). Class B (colour, §3.5): with --cpu, eco is held to it on the programme signal and on two full-drive worst cases; standard and high are reported, over it. With --cpu-calibrate (the nightly runner), the bars scale with the reference kernel, and eco's p99.9 in kernels is held to p999_kernels (its worst case on any measured machine: 1.53, EPYC 7763) x 1.15 (brain/research/native-tube-n2.md, The gate). Noise and hum (slice 5, ADR-0011 §3.2 last row): the stage's output noise density (10 Hz-40 kHz), the supply's reservoir ripple (harmonics of twice the mains at or above hum.floor_dbc) and the reservoir-to-load transfer, each against ngspice on the same circuit (tests/spice-noise/); the processor's noise in third-octave bands 25 Hz-16 kHz (60 s, Welch) and its hum harmonics against those references; 0 % digitally silent, 100 % deterministic (brain/research/native-noise-hum-n2.md).
